original.text: Whoever dishonestly receives or retains any stolen property, knowing or having reason to believe the same to be stolen property, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

Section 317: Stolen property.
Whoever dishonestly receives or retains any stolen property, knowing or having reason to believe the same to be stolen property, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

original.text: Whoever habitually receives or deals in property which he knows or has reason to believe to be stolen property, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

original.text: Whoever dishonestly receives or retains any stolen property, the possession whereof he knows or has reason to believe to have been transferred by the commission of dacoity, or dishonestly receives from a person, whom he knows or has reason to believe to belong or to have belonged to a gang of dacoits, property which he knows or has reason to believe to have been stolen, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

original.text: Property, the possession whereof has been transferred by theft or extortion or robbery or cheating, and property which has been criminally misappropriated or in respect of which criminal breach of trust has been committed, is designated as stolen property, whether the transfer has been made, or the misappropriation or breach of trust has been committed, within or without India, but, if such property subsequently comes into the possession of a person legally entitled to the possession thereof, it then ceases to be stolen property.

phase11.final_answer: A person knowingly buying stolen property may be charged under Section 317(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.
phase11.summary_answer: A person who knowingly buys stolen property may be charged under Section 317(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, for dishonestly receiving or retaining stolen property.
phase11.detailed_answer: Under Section 317(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, a person who dishonestly receives or retains any stolen property, knowing or having reason to believe it to be stolen, is subject to punishment. The penalty can include imprisonment for up to three years, a fine, or both. This applies specifically to individuals who knowingly buy stolen property.
